title: Pathfinder: staged evaluation safety pathway for A/B and progressive rollouts with automatic reversion playbooks
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a robust safety pathway (Pathfinder) that gates A/B experiments and staged canary rollouts using a combination of hypothesis-driven probes, dual-metric stability checks, and automated reversion playbooks. Pathfinder should integrate with the Evaluations service, Redwood Console dashboards, and the rollout controller to enable: 1) configurable probe sets per rollout target (cohort, region, model-variant), 2) multi-metric guards with hysteresis and confidence thresholds, 3) automatic rollback with human-notify playbooks and root-cause tagging, and 4) shadow probing and drift detection to catch latent regressions.

Acceptance Criteria:
- New rollout policy type "pathfinder-safety" available in API and Console with JSON schema and examples.
- Canary and A/B routes can reference probe-sets (text-generation prompts + evaluation metrics) stored in Evals catalog.
- Controller will evaluate metrics every minute during staged exposure, apply hysteresis window (configurable), and mark phases as FAIL/PASS using statistical tests (bootstrap CI + threshold delta).
- On FAIL, controller triggers an automatic reversion workflow: traffic rollback, incident note, create GitHub revert PR link, and notify on PagerDuty + Slack channel with playbook link.
- Console shows per-cohort metric timeline, live CI bands, and suggested rollback reasons (latency spike, quality regression, safety signal).
- Integration tests cover a synthetic outfit: simulated drift, false-positive suppression via significance windows, and no more than 0.5% false reverts in 10k simulated rollouts.

Non-Goals:
- Not replacing existing release manager UIs; this is a runtime policy + controller + eval integration.
- Not addressing manual long-running experiment analysis (postmortem analytics is separate).

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Use a lightweight statistical engine in the controller for on-path decisions (bootstrap + Bayesian smoothing), but stream raw observations to Evals aggregation for offline analysis to avoid blocking decisions on heavy computation.
- Hysteresis chosen over single-threshold to reduce flapping on noisy signals. Default hysteresis window 3 contiguous check intervals; configurable per rollout.
- To limit blast radius, first-phase exposure defaults to 1% traffic with phased doubling rules; require explicit opt-in for faster ramps.
- Automatic reversion will annotate the rollout with a snapshot of model/config, commit hash, and eval provenance to aid debugging.
